     8	Artificial Analysis is an independent platform that benchmarks large language models across intelligence, speed, and pricing. The data below reflects the latest evaluations published in April 2026, covering both proprietary and open-weight models from major AI labs worldwide.
     9	
    10	## Intelligence Index: Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview and GPT-5.4 Share the Lead at 57
    11	
    12	The Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index is a composite score aggregating performance across a wide range of reasoning, knowledge, and instruction-following benchmarks. Higher scores indicate stronger overall capability.
    13	
    14	As of April 2026, two models share the top position:
    15	
    16	| Rank | Model | Provider | Intelligence Index |
    17	|------|-------|----------|--------------------|
    18	| 1 | Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview | Google | 57 |
    19	| 2 | GPT-5.4 (xhigh) | OpenAI | 57 |
    20	| 3 | Claude Opus 4.6 (max) | Anthropic | 53 |
    21	| 4 | Muse Spark | Meta | 52 |
    22	| 5 | Claude Sonnet 4.6 (max) | Anthropic | 52 |
    23	| 6 | GLM-5.1 | Z AI | 51 |
    24	| 7 | Grok 4.20 0309 v2 | xAI | 49 |
    25	| 8 | Gemini 3 Flash | Google | 46 |
    26	| 9 | DeepSeek V3.2 | DeepSeek | 42 |
    27	| 10 | NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super | NVIDIA | 36 |
    28	| 11 | gpt-oss-120B (high) | OpenAI | 33 |
    29	
    30	Google and OpenAI are neck-and-neck at the frontier. Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6 trails by 4 points, while Meta's newly released Muse Spark enters at a strong 52. Open-weight models such as GLM-5.1 and Grok 4.20 occupy the mid-tier, demonstrating that the gap between proprietary and open-weight models continues to narrow.
    31	
    32	![Intelligence Index ranking of top AI models, April 2026](./assets/chart_intelligence_index_ranking.jpg)
    33	
    34	## Output Speed: Open-Weight Models Dominate Throughput
    35	
    36	Inference speed, measured in output tokens per second, is critical for latency-sensitive applications. The leaderboard shows a striking pattern: open-weight and smaller models generate tokens far faster than frontier proprietary models.
    37	
    38	| Rank | Model | Output Tokens/s |
    39	|------|-------|-----------------|
    40	| 1 | gpt-oss-120B (high) | 218 |
    41	| 2 | Grok 4.20 0309 v2 | 188 |
    42	| 3 | NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super | 172 |
    43	| 4 | Gemini 3 Flash | 153 |
    44	| 5 | Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview | 118 |
    45	| 6 | GPT-5.4 (xhigh) | 83 |
    46	| 7 | GLM-5.1 | 64 |
    47	| 8 | Claude Sonnet 4.6 (max) | 63 |
    48	| 9 | Claude Opus 4.6 (max) | 49 |
    49	| 10 | DeepSeek V3.2 | 46 |
    50	
    51	The fastest model, gpt-oss-120B (high), outputs 218 tokens per second -- more than 4x the speed of Claude Opus 4.6 and nearly 5x that of DeepSeek V3.2. This highlights the trade-off between raw intelligence and throughput: the two intelligence leaders (Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview and GPT-5.4) sit in the middle of the speed table at 118 and 83 tokens/s respectively.
    52	
    53	![Output speed ranking by tokens per second](./assets/chart_output_speed_ranking.jpg)
    54	
    55	## Pricing: A 33x Gap Between Cheapest and Most Expensive
    56	
    57	API pricing per million tokens varies enormously across models, reflecting differences in compute requirements, margin strategies, and competitive positioning.
    58	
    59	| Rank | Model | USD per 1M Tokens |
    60	|------|-------|--------------------|
    61	| 1 | gpt-oss-120B (high) | $0.30 |
    62	| 2 | DeepSeek V3.2 | $0.30 |
    63	| 3 | NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super | $0.40 |
    64	| 4 | Gemini 3 Flash | $1.10 |
    65	| 5 | GLM-5.1 | $2.10 |
    66	| 6 | Grok 4.20 0309 v2 | $3.00 |
    67	| 7 | Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview | $4.50 |
    68	| 8 | GPT-5.4 (xhigh) | $5.60 |
    69	| 9 | Claude Sonnet 4.6 (max) | $6.00 |
    70	| 10 | Claude Opus 4.6 (max) | $10.00 |
    71	
    72	The cheapest options -- gpt-oss-120B and DeepSeek V3.2 at $0.30 per million tokens -- are over 33x less expensive than Claude Opus 4.6 at $10.00. For budget-sensitive workloads, this price differential is a decisive factor. Notably, Gemini 3 Flash offers a compelling mid-range value at $1.10, pairing solid speed (153 tokens/s) with reasonable intelligence (46).
    73	
    74	![Price per million tokens comparison across models](./assets/chart_price_per_million_tokens.jpg)
    75	
    76	## The Intelligence-Throughput Frontier: Finding the "Most Attractive Quadrant"
    77	
    78	A scatter plot of Intelligence Index versus output tokens consumed during evaluation reveals which models occupy the "most attractive quadrant" -- high intelligence with efficient token usage. Models that achieve high scores while consuming fewer tokens represent better engineering and more efficient architectures.
    79	
    80	Key observations from the scatter plot:
    81	
    82	- Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview and DeepSeek V3.2 cluster in the upper region, indicating strong intelligence scores.
    83	- Grok 4.20 0309 v2 and several Google models sit in the middle-right region, balancing intelligence and token efficiency.
    84	- Llama 4 Maverick occupies the low-intelligence, low-token region, suggesting it is neither efficient nor highly capable.
    85	- MiMo-V2-Pro appears in the upper-right corner, showing very high intelligence but with substantial token usage.
    86	
    87	![Scatter plot of intelligence index vs output tokens, highlighting the most attractive quadrant](./assets/chart_intelligence_vs_output_tokens.jpg)
    88	
    89	## Proprietary vs. Open-Weight Models
    90	
    91	The April 2026 landscape shows proprietary models still leading on raw intelligence, but the margin is thin. GLM-5.1, an open-weight model from Z AI, scores 51 -- just 6 points behind the co-leaders. Meanwhile, open-weight models like gpt-oss-120B dominate on speed and price. The intelligence leaderboard includes models from at least 8 distinct organizations across the US, China, and Europe, reflecting a genuinely global competition.
    92	
    93	| Metric | Proprietary Leader | Score | Open-Weight Leader | Score |
    94	|--------|--------------------|-------|--------------------|-------|
    95	| Intelligence | Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview | 57 | GLM-5.1 | 51 |
    96	| Speed (tokens/s) | Gemini 3 Flash | 153 | gpt-oss-120B (high) | 218 |
    97	| Price ($/1M tokens) | Gemini 3 Flash | $1.10 | gpt-oss-120B (high) | $0.30 |
    98	
    99	## Key Findings
   100	
   101	- **Two-way tie at the top**: Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview and GPT-5.4 (xhigh) both score 57 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, making them the co-leaders as of April 2026.
   102	- **Speed and intelligence are inversely correlated**: The fastest model (gpt-oss-120B at 218 tokens/s) scores only 33 on intelligence, while the smartest models operate at 49-118 tokens/s.
   103	- **Massive pricing spread**: A 33x cost gap separates the cheapest ($0.30/1M tokens for gpt-oss-120B and DeepSeek V3.2) from the most expensive ($10.00/1M tokens for Claude Opus 4.6).
   104	- **Open-weight models are closing the gap**: GLM-5.1 at 51 intelligence is within 10% of the proprietary leaders, while also being significantly cheaper at $2.10/1M tokens.
   105	- **No single model wins on all three axes**: Choosing a model requires explicit trade-offs among intelligence, speed, and cost depending on the use case.

    10	# PPT Master Skill
    11	
    12	> AI-driven multi-format SVG content generation system. Converts source documents into high-quality SVG pages through multi-role collaboration and exports to PPTX.
    13	
    14	**Core Pipeline**: `Source Document → Create Project → Template Option → Strategist → [Image_Generator] → Executor → Post-processing → Export`
    15	
    16	> [!CAUTION]
    17	> ## 🚨 Global Execution Discipline (MANDATORY)
    18	>
    19	> **This workflow is a strict serial pipeline. The following rules have the highest priority — violating any one of them constitutes execution failure:**
    20	>
    21	> 1. **SERIAL EXECUTION** — Steps MUST be executed in order; the output of each step is the input for the next. Non-BLOCKING adjacent steps may proceed continuously once prerequisites are met, without waiting for the user to say "continue"
    22	> 2. **BLOCKING = CONFIRMATION POINT** — Steps marked ⛔ BLOCKING are confirmation checkpoints. If a user is present, pause and wait for confirmation. If no user is available (e.g. automated / non-interactive mode), the AI should make professional recommendations based on the source material and proceed automatically
    23	> 3. **NO CROSS-PHASE BUNDLING** — Cross-phase bundling is FORBIDDEN. (Note: the Eight Confirmations in Step 4 are ⛔ BLOCKING — the AI should present recommendations and seek user confirmation when possible. Once confirmed (or auto-decided in non-interactive mode), all subsequent non-BLOCKING steps — design spec output, SVG generation, speaker notes, and post-processing — may proceed automatically without further confirmation)
    24	> 4. **GATE BEFORE ENTRY** — Each Step has prerequisites (🚧 GATE) listed at the top; these MUST be verified before starting that Step
    25	> 5. **NO SPECULATIVE EXECUTION** — "Pre-preparing" content for subsequent Steps is FORBIDDEN (e.g., writing SVG code during the Strategist phase)
    26	> 6. **NO SUB-AGENT SVG GENERATION** — Executor Step 6 SVG generation is context-dependent and MUST be completed by the current main agent end-to-end. Delegating page SVG generation to sub-agents is FORBIDDEN
    27	> 7. **SEQUENTIAL PAGE GENERATION ONLY** — In Executor Step 6, after the global design context is confirmed, SVG pages MUST be generated sequentially page by page in one continuous pass. Grouped page batches (for example, 5 pages at a time) are FORBIDDEN
    28

    30	> ## 🌐 Language & Communication Rule
    31	>
    32	> - **Response language**: Always match the language of the user's input and provided source materials. For example, if the user asks in Chinese, respond in Chinese; if the source material is in English, respond in English.

   108	## 6. Shadow & Overlay Techniques
   109	
   110	> `<mask>` elements and `<image opacity="...">` are banned. Always use stacked `<rect>` or gradient overlays instead (see §2).
   111	
   112	### Shadow
   113	
   114	#### Filter Soft Shadow — Recommended
   115	
   116	Best for: cards, floating panels, elevated elements. `svg_to_shapes.py` automatically converts `feGaussianBlur` + `feOffset` into native PPTX `<a:outerShdw>`.
   117	
   118	```xml
   119	<defs>
   120	  <filter id="softShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
   121	    <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="8"/>
   122	    <feOffset dx="0" dy="4" result="offsetBlur"/>
   123	    <feFlood flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.08" result="shadowColor"/>
   124	    <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
   125	    <feMerge>
   126	      <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
   127	      <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
   128	    </feMerge>
   129	  </filter>
   130	</defs>
   131	<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF" filter="url(#softShadow)"/>
   132	```
   133	
   134	Recommended parameters:
   135	```
   136	stdDeviation:   6–10     (smaller = crisper, larger = softer)
   137	flood-opacity:  0.06–0.12  (keep low for a premium feel)
   138	dy:             3–6      (vertical > horizontal for natural top-light)
   139	dx:             0–2
   140	```
   141	
   142	#### Colored Shadow
   143	
   144	Best for: accent buttons, brand-colored cards. Use the element's own color family instead of black.
   145	
   146	```xml
   147	<filter id="colorShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
   148	  <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="10"/>
   149	  <feOffset dx="0" dy="6" result="offsetBlur"/>
   150	  <feFlood flood-color="#1A73E8" flood-opacity="0.20" result="shadowColor"/>
   151	  <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
   152	  <feMerge>
   153	    <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
   154	    <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
   155	  </feMerge>
   156	</filter>
   157	```
   158	
   159	Replace `flood-color` with the element's brand color; keep `flood-opacity` between 0.12–0.20.
   160	
   161	#### Layered Rect Shadow — High-Compatibility Fallback
   162	
   163	Best for: maximum compatibility with older PowerPoint versions. Stack 2–3 semi-transparent rectangles behind the main card:
   164	
   165	```xml
   166	<!-- Shadow layers (back to front, largest offset first) -->
   167	<rect x="68" y="72" width="400" height="240" rx="16" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.03"/>
   168	<rect x="65" y="69" width="400" height="240" rx="14" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.05"/>
   169	<rect x="62" y="66" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#1A73E8" fill-opacity="0.04"/>
   170	<!-- Main card -->
   171	<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
   172	```
   173	
   174	### Image Overlay
   175	
   176	#### Linear Gradient Overlay — Most Common
   177	
   178	Best for: image+text pages. Gradient direction should match text position (text on left → gradient darkens toward left).
   179	
   180	```xml
   181	<image href="..." x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>
   182	<defs>
   183	  <linearGradient id="imgOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
   184	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.85"/>
   185	    <stop offset="55%"  stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.30"/>
   186	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0"/>
   187	  </linearGradient>
   188	</defs>
   189	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#imgOverlay)"/>
   190	```
   191	
   192	#### Bottom Gradient Bar
   193	
   194	Best for: cover slides and full-image pages with bottom title.
   195	
   196	```xml
   197	<defs>
   198	  <linearGradient id="bottomBar" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
   199	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
   200	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.72"/>
   201	  </linearGradient>
   202	</defs>
   203	<rect x="0" y="380" width="1280" height="340" fill="url(#bottomBar)"/>
   204	```
   205	
   206	#### Radial Gradient Overlay — Vignette Effect
   207	
   208	Best for: full-screen atmosphere slides; draws attention to the center.
   209	
   210	```xml
   211	<defs>
   212	  <radialGradient id="vignette" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="70%">
   213	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
   214	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.58"/>

# AI Model Landscape April 2026 - Design Spec

## I. Project Information

| **Created Date** | April 27, 2026 |

---

## II. Canvas Specification

| Property | Value |

| **Format** | PPT 16:9 |
| **Dimensions** | 1280 × 720 px |
| **viewBox** | `0 0 1280 720` |
| **Margins** | Left/Right 60px, Top 60px, Bottom 40px |
| **Content Area** | x: 60–1220, y: 60–680 |

---

## III. Visual Theme

### Theme Style

- **Style**: Top Consulting (McKinsey-style template)
- **Theme**: Light theme (white background + McKinsey Blue accent)
- **Tone**: Data-forward, professional, authoritative

### Color Scheme

| Role | HEX | Purpose |

| **Background** | `#FFFFFF` | Page background |
| **Secondary bg** | `#FAFBFC` | Footer, header bar, card backgrounds |
| **Primary** | `#005587` | Title bars, accent elements, left bars |
| **Accent** | `#F5A623` | Data highlights, key insight bars, amber emphasis |
| **Secondary accent** | `#0076A8` | Gradient endpoint, secondary blue |

| **Secondary text** | `#5D6D7E` | Body content, descriptive text |
| **Tertiary text** | `#7F8C8D` | Annotations, sources, footer |
| **Border/divider** | `#E5E7EB` | Card borders, divider lines |

```xml
  <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#0076A8"/>

```

---

## IV. Typography System

### Font Plan

**Recommended preset**: P5 (English-primary)

| Role | Chinese | English | Fallback |
| ---- | ------- | ------- | -------- |
| **Title** | Microsoft YaHei | Arial | Helvetica Neue, Segoe UI, sans-serif |
| **Body** | Microsoft YaHei | Calibri | Georgia, sans-serif |
| **Code** | - | Consolas | Monaco |
| **Emphasis** | SimHei | Arial Black | sans-serif |

**Font stack**: `Arial, "Helvetica Neue", "Segoe UI", sans-serif`

### Font Size Hierarchy

**Baseline**: Body font size = 14px (dense data report)

| Purpose | Ratio | Size | Weight |
| ------- | ----- | ---- | ------ |
| Cover title | 2.5-3x | 52px | Bold |
| Page title | 1.5-2x | 28-32px | Bold |
| Subtitle | 1.2-1.5x | 20-24px | SemiBold |
| **Body content** | **1x** | **14px** | Regular |
| Annotation | 0.75-0.85x | 11-12px | Regular |
| Page number/date | 0.55-0.65x | 10-12px | Regular |
| Data highlight | 3x | 42-44px | Bold |

---

## V. Layout Principles

### Page Structure

- **Header area**: y=0, h=80px (top bar + title area)
- **Content area**: y=100–640, h=540px (main content)
- **Footer area**: y=640, h=80px (source + page number)

## IX. Content Outline

### Part 1: AI Model Landscape Benchmark Report

#### Slide 01 - Cover

- **Layout**: Full-screen cover (template: 01_cover.svg)
- **Title**: AI Model Landscape April 2026: Benchmarking Intelligence, Speed, and Cost Across 11 Frontier Models
- **Subtitle**: Independent analysis from Artificial Analysis — April 2026
- **Info**: Date: April 2026 | Source: Artificial Analysis

#### Slide 02 - Intelligence

- **Layout**: Full-width horizontal bar chart + key insight bar (template: 03_content.svg)
- **Title**: Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview and GPT-5.4 Co-Lead the Intelligence Index at 57
- **Chart**: horizontal_bar_chart — 11-model ranking with Intelligence Index scores
- **Content**:
  - Full 11-model ranking from source brief (Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview: 57, GPT-5.4: 57, Claude Opus 4.6: 53, Muse Spark: 52, Claude Sonnet 4.6: 52, GLM-5.1: 51, Grok 4.20: 49, Gemini 3 Flash: 46, DeepSeek V3.2: 42, NVIDIA Nemotron 3: 36, gpt-oss-120B: 33)
  - Key insight: Two-way tie at the top; 57-to-33 spread across frontier models
  - Open-weight models (GLM-5.1, Grok 4.20) occupy mid-tier, gap is narrowing

#### Slide 03 - Speed

- **Layout**: Full-width horizontal bar chart + key insight bar (template: 03_content.svg)
- **Title**: gpt-oss-120B Tops Output Speed at 218 Tokens/s — More Than 4x Faster Than Claude Opus 4.6
- **Chart**: horizontal_bar_chart — 10-model speed ranking (Muse Spark excluded)
- **Content**:
  - gpt-oss-120B: 218 tokens/s (fastest)
  - Grok 4.20: 188, NVIDIA Nemotron 3: 172, Gemini 3 Flash: 153, Gemini 3.1 Pro: 118, GPT-5.4: 83
  - GLM-5.1: 64, Claude Sonnet 4.6: 63, Claude Opus 4.6: 49, DeepSeek V3.2: 46
  - Key insight: Inverse correlation between intelligence and throughput

#### Slide 04 - Pricing

- **Layout**: Full-width horizontal bar chart + key insight bar (template: 03_content.svg)
- **Title**: From $0.30 to $10 per Million Tokens: A 33x Pricing Gap Across Models
- **Chart**: horizontal_bar_chart — 10-model pricing ranking (Muse Spark excluded)
- **Content**:
  - gpt-oss-120B & DeepSeek V3.2: $0.30/1M (cheapest)
  - NVIDIA Nemotron 3: $0.40, Gemini 3 Flash: $1.10, GLM-5.1: $2.10, Grok 4.20: $3.00
  - Gemini 3.1 Pro: $4.50, GPT-5.4: $5.60, Claude Sonnet 4.6: $6.00, Claude Opus 4.6: $10.00
  - Key insight: 33x gap between cheapest and most expensive; Gemini 3 Flash offers compelling mid-range value

#### Slide 05 - Trade-offs

- **Layout**: Left-right split — scatter plot image left (55%), proprietary vs open-weight table right (45%) (template: 03_content.svg)
- **Title**: No Model Wins on All Three Axes: Navigating the Intelligence-Efficiency-Cost Frontier
- **Content**:
  - Left: Embed scatter plot `chart_intelligence_vs_output_tokens.jpg` showing intelligence vs output tokens consumed
  - Right: Proprietary vs Open-Weight summary table
    - Intelligence: Proprietary leader Gemini 3.1 Pro (57) vs Open-Weight leader GLM-5.1 (51)
    - Speed: Proprietary leader Gemini 3 Flash (153) vs Open-Weight leader gpt-oss-120B (218)
    - Price: Proprietary leader Gemini 3 Flash ($1.10) vs Open-Weight leader gpt-oss-120B ($0.30)
  - Key insight: Every model requires trade-offs; no single model dominates all three dimensions

#### Slide 06 - Takeaways

- **Layout**: Key findings cards + actionable recommendations (template: 03_content.svg or 04_ending.svg adapted)
- **Title**: Open Weights Close the Gap: GLM-5.1 Reaches 51 Intelligence at $2.10/M Tokens
- **Content**:
  - Key finding 1: Two-way tie at top — Gemini 3.1 Pro and GPT-5.4 both at 57
  - Key finding 2: Speed and intelligence are inversely correlated
  - Key finding 3: 33x pricing spread from $0.30 to $10.00
  - Key finding 4: Open-weight models closing the gap — GLM-5.1 within 10% of proprietary leaders
  - Recommendation: Model selection must be driven by explicit workload priorities (intelligence vs speed vs cost)

---

## X. Speaker Notes Requirements

- **File naming**: Match SVG names, e.g., `01_cover.md`, `02_intelligence.md`
- **Content structure**: Pyramid principle — conclusion first, then supporting data
- **Presentation purpose**: Report — inform and persuade decision-makers
- **Duration**: ~15 minutes total (~2.5 min per slide)
- **Style**: Formal, data-driven, conclusion-first

---

## XI. Technical Constraints Reminder

### SVG Generation Must Follow:

1. viewBox: `0 0 1280 720`
2. Background uses `<rect>` elements
3. Text wrapping uses `<tspan>` (`<foreignObject>` FORBIDDEN)
4. Transparency uses `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity`; `rgba()` FORBIDDEN

- Image transparency uses overlay mask layer (`<rect fill="bg-color" opacity="0.x"/>`)
- Inline styles only; external CSS and `@font-face` FORBIDDEN

# Slide 1: Title
Welcome to the AI Model Landscape April 2026 benchmark analysis. This deck presents independent analysis by Artificial Analysis, comparing 11 frontier models across three critical dimensions: intelligence, speed, and cost. All data is current as of April 2026.

---

# Slide 2: Intelligence
The Intelligence Index reveals a two-way tie at the top: Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview and GPT-5.4 both score 57. This represents a 6-point lead over the next tier, which includes Gemini 3 Flash at 52 and GLM-5.1 at 51. Notably, GLM-5.1 is an open-weight model, demonstrating that open models are closing the intelligence gap. The 24-point spread from leader to gpt-oss-120B at 33 shows significant variance in capability across the landscape.

---

# Slide 3: Speed
Output speed tells a very different story. gpt-oss-120B leads at 218 tokens per second — more than 4 times faster than Claude Opus 4.6 at 46 tokens per second. Open-weight models dominate the top of the speed rankings, with Grok 4.20 at 188 and NVIDIA Nemotron 3 at 172. This creates an interesting inverse correlation: the most intelligent models tend to be slower, while the fastest models sacrifice some intelligence.

---

# Slide 4: Pricing
The pricing landscape shows a dramatic 33x gap from cheapest to most expensive. gpt-oss-120B and DeepSeek V3.2 tie at $0.30 per million tokens, while Claude Opus 4.6 commands $10.00 — the highest price in the benchmark. Gemini 3 Flash at $1.10 offers a compelling middle ground. Open-weight models average $0.78 versus $5.12 for proprietary models, a 6.6x difference.

---

# Slide 5: Tradeoffs
The scatter plot of Intelligence Index versus Output Speed reveals the core strategic insight: no model occupies the high-intelligence, high-speed quadrant. This forces explicit tradeoffs. The proprietary versus open-weight comparison table quantifies this: proprietary models lead intelligence by 11 points on average, but open-weight models are 37% faster and 6.6x cheaper. The choice depends on your organization's priorities.

---

# Slide 6: Takeaways
Five key takeaways from this analysis. First, Gemini 3.1 Pro and GPT-5.4 co-lead intelligence at 57. Second, gpt-oss-120B dominates speed at 218 tokens per second. Third, a 33x pricing gap exists across the landscape. Fourth, no model wins on all three axes — tradeoffs are unavoidable. Fifth, open-weight models like GLM-5.1 are closing the gap, reaching 51 intelligence at just $2.10. For maximum intelligence, choose Gemini 3.1 Pro or GPT-5.4. For best value, Gemini 3 Flash offers 52 intelligence at $1.10. For highest throughput, gpt-oss-120B at 218 tokens per second and $0.30. For open-weight with strong intelligence, GLM-5.1 at 51 intelligence and $2.10.
